column3: The Hebrew repeats the keeping root in keeping His charge and says “all the days”; BSB says “keep His charge” and “always.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names the LORD in the destruction clause; BSB uses “He.” The sea’s Hebrew name means “Sea of Reeds,” while BSB has “Red Sea.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew identifies Eliab as “son of Reuben” and places the living things “at their feet”; BSB has “the Reubenite” and “that belonged to them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “the whole commandment” and does not explicitly name the Jordan here; BSB has “every commandment” and supplies “the Jordan.”
The Hebrew uses “their seed”; BSB says “their descendants.”
The Hebrew says “with your foot”; BSB says “on foot.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly name the Jordan here and says the land drinks water from the rain of heaven; BSB supplies “the Jordan” and says it “drinks in the rain.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says “My commandments”; BSB says “the commandments.”
The Hebrew names the early and latter rains; BSB identifies these as “the autumn and spring rains.”
The Hebrew has singular “your field”; BSB has plural “the fields.”
The Hebrew names “your heart” as what may be enticed; BSB says “you are not enticed.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew says to put the words “on” heart and soul, calls the hand a singular “your hand,” and places the frontlets “between your eyes.” BSB has “in your hearts and minds,” plural “hands,” and “on your foreheads.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has singular “your house”; BSB has plural “your houses.”
The Hebrew repeats “days” for the children and for the heavens above the earth; BSB uses “those” for the children and recasts the final comparison as “as long as.”
The Hebrew uses singular “this whole commandment”; BSB uses plural “all these commandments.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “river” before naming the Euphrates and calls the sea “the rear sea”; BSB names the river once and says “the Western Sea.”

The Hebrew says to “put” the blessing and curse on the mountains; BSB says to “proclaim” them.
The Hebrew uses plural “oaks of Moreh” and a singular collective name for the Canaanite; BSB has singular “the Oak of Moreh” and plural “Canaanites.”
